She erased the location of Earth, though it would be thousands of years before humanity sent another ship back to the area that this one had already explored, She erased it, and transferred her own memories to the pittance of ship’s memory left. Humanity would condemn her for the selfish decision, and she was ashamed of herself. She felt weak, and not because of the pathogens— though they were attacking her proxy body with vigor.

She had been infected by Celtiberian’s damned idiosyncrasies, his damned curiosity, his damned self-love, and she'd sacrificed the mission for the survival of her own memories. She was angry—angry, like no human had been for thousands of generations—angry at herself and angry at Celtiberian for giving her the ability to feel anger.

She unleashed the anger on the infection, digging at it, attacking it even as the antibodies attacked her. She ripped at the infection, ignoring her own disintegrating proxy body, ignoring the weakening of her arms, ignoring the little pieces of wrenched tissue as the antibodies digested her. Soon, she was flailing at nothing but the flowing blood. Soon, she could not hold onto the wall, soon her limbs began to fall apart, and she broke up into fragments, carried off by the blood to be reabsorbed by the ship’s liver. She lost consciousness and died once more in the blood stream.
